output:

Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Great tub, one indoor flood, get your warranty terms in writing

3 stars

I'm a mobile dog groomer in Halifax, and Harbourline did the grooming fitout on my Transit this past August: tub, ramp, water tanks, on-demand water heater, floor, cabinets, the works.

Good stuff first, because it really is good. The stainless tub and ramp are honestly the best thing about my van. Dogs walk right in on their own, including the big guys who would otherwise need a forklift and a signed waiver.

Now, October 27. About ten weeks after pickup, I'm mid-groom in Bedford with Moose, a 110 lb Bernese, in the tub, and a fitting on the hot water line lets go. Water all over the floor and down into the cabinet. I was screaming. Moose was not. Moose sat in that tub through the entire flood like a king having a fountain installed. I towelled him off and sent him home half done, one side fluffy and one side not. His owner tells me he thinks it was a pool party, so at least one of us had a nice day.

Here's why this is 3 stars and not 4 or 5. The leak itself isn't what made me mad. Stuff breaks, I get it. What got me was the reply the next day: these lines don't just let go, it's usually because the heater's been run dry or someone's been hanging stuff off the pipe, so that would be user error and not covered. Plus a $180 diagnostic fee to look at it, and the earliest they could get me in was Nov 3. For the record, I have never run that heater dry, and the pipe is behind a cabinet door. Nobody is hanging anything off it. Not even Moose.

All in, the van was off the road from Oct 27 to Nov 6. That cost me the rest of that day plus six bookings, which is a rough week and a half when the van is the whole business.

Credit where it's due, though. Once Glenn got in there, he found the compression fitting on the heater outlet was a cheaper one his supplier had swapped in. He told me straight that it was on them, replaced all the fittings on the hot side and not only the one that failed, and the $180 went away. He owned it in the end and I want that on the record as much as the rest of it.

If you're a groomer or a trade looking at Harbourline, here's my advice. The work you can see is solid and I'd still take that tub over any other I've used. But the invoice says "12 month workmanship warranty, excludes damage from misuse or user error," and that one line turned out to matter a lot. Before you pay, get it in writing:

- what actually counts as user error, and who decides
- whether you owe a diagnostic fee if the problem turns out to be theirs
- how fast they'll get you in when the vehicle is your income

If I'd had that on paper, this would have been a much shorter, much more boring story, and probably a 4 star review.

Moose, for what it's worth, gives it five.
